source_text: III. Advenientes vero parentes eius, videntes eum torqueri precabantur eum, hinc pueri pedes eius amplectentes dicebant: Miserere tui et nostri, pater; inde uxores lugentes vultum et aetatem eius precabantur. parentum vero omnium luctus et fletus erat super eum, domesticorum gemitus, vicinorum ululatus et lamentatio amicorum, qui omnes clamantes ad eum dicebant: Tenerae adolescentiae tuae miserere. sed, ut dictum est, meliore cupiditate detentus, sententiam domini ante oculos habens, quae dixit: Si quis me negaverit coram hominibus, et ego negabo eum coram patre meo qui in caelis est: omnes ergo despiciens nulli eorum respondit. festinabat enim ad supernae spem vocationis pervenire. Probus praeses dixit: Quid dicis? flectere horum lacrymis ab insania tua et consulens adolescentiae tuae sacrifica. Irenaeus respondit: Consulo mihi in perpetuum, si non sacrificavero. Probus iussit eum recipi in custodiam carceris. plurimis vero diebus ibidem clausus diversis poenis est affectus.
thought_title: Family pleading and refusal to answer
orientation: Irenaeus has refused to offer sacrifice under torture, and now his parents and children and wives and household and neighbours and friends beg him to spare his youth while Governor Probus again urges him to offer sacrifice.
pass_a_gloss: But his parents coming, seeing him being tortured, were begging him, on one side children embracing his feet saying: Have mercy on yourself and on us, father; on the other side wives mourning were begging his face and his age. But of all the parents there was grief and weeping over him, groaning of members of the household, wailing of neighbours and lament of friends, who all shouting to him were saying: Have mercy on your tender youth. But, as it has been said, held by a better desire, having before his eyes the saying of the Lord, which said: If anyone denies me before men, I also will deny him before my Father who is in the heavens: therefore looking down on all he answered to none of them. For he was hastening to arrive at the hope of the heavenly calling. Probus the governor said: What do you say? Be bent by the tears of these from your madness and looking out for your youth offer sacrifice. Irenaeus answered: I look out for myself for ever, if I do not offer sacrifice. Probus ordered him to be received into the guard of the prison. But shut up in the same place for very many days he was afflicted with diverse punishments.

choices.why: work brief glossary fixes sacrificare as offer sacrifice for the required pagan loyalty test
work brief glossary fixes negare as deny for disowning Christ to escape death
work brief glossary fixes praeses as governor for the Roman judge
source is plural so literal lane keeps plural even though the brief cast lists wife among family pleaders

bible_refs.note: Si quis me negaverit coram hominibus, et ego negabo eum coram patre meo qui in caelis est

pass_b_english: Then his parents came and saw him under torture and begged him to yield. His children clung to his feet and said, "Have pity on yourself and on us, father." His wives mourned over his face and his youth as they pleaded with him. Grief and weeping from all his parents hung over him, groaning from his household, wailing from his neighbours, and lamentation from his friends, and they all cried out to him together, "Have pity on your tender youth."

But, as has been said, Irenaeus was held by a stronger longing and kept before his eyes the sentence of the Lord, who said, "Whoever denies me before men, I also will deny him before my Father who is in heaven" (Matthew 10:33). So he looked past them all and answered none of them, for he was hurrying to reach the hope of his heavenly calling.

Probus the governor said, "What do you say? Let their tears turn you from your madness, think of your youth, and offer sacrifice." Irenaeus answered, "I am thinking of myself for eternity if I do not offer sacrifice." So Probus ordered him to be taken back into the custody of the prison, and after he had been shut there for many days he was afflicted with various punishments.
